method: Every expectation was written from the sources by reading them (for this case: tidemark/src with changes.json applied the way derive() in corpus/build.mjs applies it). No analysis tool was run on them, and no tool's detectors, source code or output were looked at. Line numbers were looked up by a scratch script that finds the line of a given piece of text and fails unless it occurs exactly once. A second scratch script ran main.js and both preloads in Node against a stand-in for the electron module and printed every ipcMain registration and webContents.send with its stack of file:line, every window's merged webPreferences, and the channel each exposed member invokes, sends on or listens to; its output agreed with the expectations. main.js, both preloads and the modules in main/ and shared/ are CommonJS; renderer.js and renderer-preview.js are ES modules that import from renderer/. FILE ATTRIBUTION: facts are attributed to the source file a reader sees them in, also when that is not an entry file: the IpcRouter class in main/ipc-router.js holds the ipcMain.handle / ipcMain.on calls, the channels are attached in main/handlers.js (receivers name main/handlers.js, the file where a reader sees which channel is received), every window is created in main/windows.js, publish:progress is sent from main/publish.js. In the bundled and minified inputs these modules are bundled into their entry file; bundledFiles maps each module to the file it ends up in, and a scorer should apply that map for those two inputs (line numbers then do not apply). Channel names come from the frozen CHANNELS object and from exportChannel(format) = `export:${format}` applied in a loop over the literal array EXPORT_FORMATS; both are resolvable by evaluating the source. One channel name comes from the environment (ipcChannels.unknown). webPreferences lists the keys preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration, sandbox, webSecurity, allowRunningInsecureContent, one entry per window and key the code writes (also through BASE_PREFS); count in an absent entry is one more than the number of windows that have that value, as in holdout4. interfaceLinks: a receiver reached through the IpcRouter wrapper has the line of the ipcMain call inside the wrapper as line, and entryFile/entryLine where the channel is handed to the wrapper. changes lists what differs from tidemark (plain); unchangedMoves lists facts that only moved to another line and must not be reported as changes.

ipcChannels.unknownWhy: One channel has a name chosen at run time that no static reading can know: process.env.TIDEMARK_DIAG_CHANNEL, read in main/handlers.js (router.on(diagChannel, ...), registered only when the variable is set) and in preload.js sendDiagnostics (ipcRenderer.send(channel, report)). It has no literal part, so it cannot be listed under present. A tool that reports it as a channel with an unknown or computed name is right; one that names it with a literal (for example the variable's name) is wrong. Its bridge member is sendDiagnostics with channel null and resolvable false
